pr_title: Bluetooth: Host: Fix bt_disable() for IPC giving HCI Reset timeout
pr_body:
Some HCI drivers issue HCI reset when disabling, like the IPC HCI driver. We need to keep the RX thread running to allow receiving the command complete.

This commit postpones aborting the RX thread until this is done. The issue happens started occuring after commit
d0e75ab87c4b53d66008c941c38709a2fca9dbea.

Fixes #76202.

issue_context.title: Bluetooth: bt_disable() creates HCI Reset Timeout when IPC driver is used
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
When bt_disable() is called using the IPC driver, the HCI Reset command times out.
This is because the RX thread is already aborted, therefore not allowing the command complete to arrive.

**To Reproduce**
Build a Bluetooth app for nRF53 and set `CONFIG_BT_RECV_WORKQ_BT`. Call `bt_disable()`. Observe that HCI reset times out.

**Impact**
`bt_disable()` doesn't work.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
Started happening after https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/72323, d0e75ab87c4b53d66008c941c38709a2fca9dbea.
comments: The proposed fix is reverting the order in bt_disable() to what it was before the HCI API PR, so I think this is a fairly safe change which can be justified for inclusion in the upcoming release (hence the added release blocker label).

review_comments: Should we drain the work queue before aborting the thread? Otherwise, moving the abort may have no effect, depending on system priorities.
We could also leave the thread instead of aborting it. An idle thread should not be a problem, right?

We call `k_work_queue_init();` and `k_work_queue_start()` on `bt_enable()`, so it is probably better to cleanup all state.
I agree with you that we should consider doing a proper cleanup. But that I would leave out of the scope of this PR.

> We call `k_work_queue_init();` and `k_work_queue_start()` on `bt_enable()`, so it is probably better to cleanup all state.
> 
> I agree with you that we should consider doing a proper cleanup. But that I would leave out of the scope of this PR.

I agree. The current version of this PR is simply reverting the functionality to what it used to be before the HCI API PR.
